interest: This file provides valuable insight into the internal State Department debates during early 1941 that preceded the decisive July 1941 freezing of Japanese assets in the United States. It highlights the sharp tension between frontline diplomats like Ambassador Joseph C. Grew, who urged immediate reciprocal asset controls to protect American corporate investments and frozen balances trapped under Japan's wartime economic controls, and the cautious posture of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs, which resisted unilateral action against Japan in the absence of a worldwide freezing policy. Additionally, the reference to Japanese capital investments in Mexican petroleum and trading companies illustrates Washington's parallel vigilance regarding Axis economic penetration in Latin America prior to Pearl Harbor.
overview: This State Department file (decimal file 894.503112, with associated papers under 812.5034 and 894.5034) documents Japanese foreign economic activities and the treatment of international capital between October 1940 and March 1941. It includes a cross-reference sheet indexing a report from Ambassador Josephus Daniels in Mexico regarding Japanese financial interests in four Mexican-registered petroleum, drug, and commercial enterprises. The file also contains an extensive policy memorandum prepared by the Division of Far Eastern Affairs for Assistant Secretary of State Dean Acheson regarding recommendations by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo to freeze Japanese assets and restrict fund transfers from the United States in retaliation for Japanese exchange controls and industrial mobilization measures that froze American corporate balances in Japan.

subfiles.summary: This cross-reference sheet indexes Despatch No. 11667 of October 25, 1940, from Ambassador Josephus Daniels in Mexico City, filed under 812.5034/147. The despatch encloses a memorandum prepared by W. Richardson concerning Japanese interests in four companies registered in Mexico: Cia. Mexicana de Petroleo 'La Laguna', S.A.; Cia. Petrolera Veracruzana, S.A.; Cia. Internacional de Drogas, S.A.; and Cia. Internacional de Comercio S.A. It references subject file 894.503112/2 regarding Japanese capital investments in Mexico.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Despatch No. 11667 from Mexico on Japanese Interests in Mexican Companies

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum evaluating Ambassador Grew's proposal to freeze Japanese assets in the United States to safeguard American corporate holdings in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Division of Far Eastern Affairs reviews Telegram No. 383 from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew in Tokyo, which reported severe anxiety among American manufacturing firms in Japan over newly enacted industrial control legislation, expropriation risks, and tight foreign exchange restrictions freezing American funds. Grew advocated taking immediate steps to control the liquidation and transfer of Japanese assets in the United States to compel the release of American holdings on a pari passu basis. The memorandum acknowledges the commercial inequity but argues against singling out Japan outside of a worldwide freezing policy, suggesting instead that Dean Acheson convene a meeting and coordinate with the Treasury Department regarding post-freezing trade arrangements and quid pro quo releases.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from the Division of Far Eastern Affairs to Dean Acheson on Freezing Japanese Assets and Protecting American Investments
